content: 1. By 2030, the goal is to achieve significant advancements in health systems globally, as discussed in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2019. 2. Fouda and Paolucci explored the concept of path dependence in achieving universal health coverage, using Egypt as a case study, published in Frontiers in Public Health in 2017. 3. A new insurance mandate in Egypt demonstrates the country's commitment to improving its healthcare system, as highlighted by the Oxford Business Group. 4. Egypt's health system profile includes key health system indicators, providing a comprehensive overview of its current state. 5. The World Health Organization (WHO) and Egypt collaborated on a country cooperation strategy for the years 2010–2014, focusing on health system improvements. 6. A nationwide initiative to enhance students' healthcare in Egyptian schools was launched, as reported by Egypt Today in 2018. 7. Schwefel analyzed health financing in Egypt, including national health accounts, health insurance, and family health funds, drawing lessons for Syria's Health Sector Modernization Programme. 8. Egypt's youth champions are actively working on implementing reproductive health policies, as detailed in a country brief series. 9. Yip and Berman examined the impact of targeted health insurance on access and equity in Egypt's school health insurance program, published in Health Economics in 2001. 10. Park et al. conducted interviews with key stakeholders to understand the school health environment in Lao PDR, Mongolia, Nepal, and Sri Lanka, published in Health Education Research in 2015. 11. The Lao People's Revolutionary Youth Union and the UN Fund for Population Activities analyzed the adolescent and youth situation in Lao PDR, emphasizing the importance of investing in young people. 12. Lao PDR's health sector reform strategy and framework, extending until 2025, outlines the country's approach to modernizing its health system. 13. Saito et al. identified factors influencing the implementation of national school health policies in Lao PDR through a multi-level case study, published in Health Promotion International in 2015. 14. The Fit for School initiative developed a school community manual for Lao PDR, providing guidelines for improving school health. 15. The Ministry of Education in Lao PDR created a national school health strategic plan to address health challenges in schools. 16. The Ministry of Education and WHO collaborated on a minimum package for school health services, aiming to standardize health interventions in schools. 17. Rwanda's fourth health sector strategic plan (2018–2024) outlines the country's priorities for improving health services. 18. Rwanda's national guidelines for school eye health screening, published in 2019, aim to address vision-related issues among students. 19. Dibakwane and Peu explored the experiences of school health nurses in delivering health services in South Africa's Tshwane district, published in the African Journal of Primary Health Care & Family Medicine in 2018. 20. Doyle et al. investigated the utilization of primary healthcare and school health services by adolescents in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, published in BMC Health Services Research in 2019. 21. The Department of Health and the Department of Basic Education in South Africa developed an integrated school health policy to enhance health service delivery in schools. 22. Rasesemola et al. examined compliance with the integrated school health policy in South Africa, focusing on intersectoral and multisectoral collaboration, published in Curationis in 2019. 23. Ardahan and Erkin studied the opinions of private and public school teachers regarding the roles of school nurses, published in the Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association in 2018. 24. Bayik Temel et al. developed a scale to measure parents' and teachers' expectations of school nurse roles, published in the International Journal of Nursing Sciences in 2017. 25. Kocoglu and Emiroglu assessed the impact of comprehensive school nursing services on students' academic performance, published in the Journal of Caring Sciences in 2017. 26. Baysal and Ince reviewed recent developments in school-based health services in Turkey, published in the Journal of Pediatric Research in 2018. 27. Yilmazel and Cetinkaya investigated health literacy among school teachers in Çorum, Turkey, published in the Eastern Mediterranean Health Journal in 2015. 28. A research brief addressed strategies for schools to meet the needs of students with chronic health conditions. 29. Brener et al. provided an overview of school health profiles in 2016, detailing the characteristics of health programs in secondary schools. 30. The 2018 school health profiles continued to document the characteristics of health programs in secondary schools. 31. The 2020 school health profiles, published by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), provided updated insights into health programs in secondary schools. 32. The CDC also released guidelines on school health services in 2020, emphasizing the importance of comprehensive health interventions in schools. 33. School-based health centers were highlighted by the Health Resources and Services Administration as critical components of student health services. 34. Carr and Modzeleski authored a primer on how schools operate and how to effectively collaborate with them to serve children and youth, published by the National Association of State Boards of Education in 2014. 35. The WHO guideline on school health services includes a web annex that reviews global school health services, their methodologies, and key findings. 36. The State Policy Database provides information on health policies relevant to school health services. 37. The Common Core of Data website offers public data and frequently asked questions about America's public schools. 38. Educational and community programs are highlighted as essential for addressing health and educational objectives. 39. Lewallen et al. introduced the Whole School, Whole Community, Whole Child model, a new approach to improving educational attainment and healthy development for students, published in the Journal of School Health in 2015.
